newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-LIMPING EDBERG LOSES OPENING DAVIS CUP MATCH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-LIMPING EDBERG LOSES OPENING DAVIS CUP MATCH.

text.p: A limping Stefan Edberg went down 6-3 6-4 6-3 to France's Cedric Pioline in the opening singles of the Davis Cup final on Friday.

Edberg, who retires on Monday after the tie, fell heavily in the sixth game of the first set and twisted his ankle. He took a three-minute time-out to have the ankle bandaged but it obviously caused him pain for the rest of the match.
Pioline, France's top player but ranked seven places below the Swede's 14th ATP ranking, took full advantage of Edberg's injury. He placed shots deep and wide, forcing his opponent to chase.
Edberg tried to keep the game to a simple serve and volley formula but made too many errors rushing the net, his face frequently contorted with pain.

Pioline, roared on by a noisy and colourful contingent of French supporters in the converted factory building used for the final, broke Edberg's serve in the eighth game of the first set after the pair had exchanged breaks earlier in the set.

He broke again in the third game of the second set, using a whipping forehand to great effect. Edberg broke back immediately but the effort proved too much for him and Pioline was able to wear down his 30-year-old opponent.
Breaks in the fifth and ninth games of the third set set up Pioline's win, Edberg finally succumbing to a lob which he could not move fast enough to retrieve.
